facts.text: The official tag resolves to exact commit 8ea63498c7aa107995f9b2ffee7789631707e09f; release publication is 2026-08-28T03:29:22Z. Source reasoning below is pinned to that commit, not to mutable main or a version-name assumption.

Response::send wraps the outgoing HTTP response as a system stream and returns jsBody.pumpTo. Its ownership comment explicitly requires the returned cancellable promise to own all response writes. This proves the intended code/ownership path, not that our RST dropped this exact promise.

The pinned JS-controller pump always constructs a DrainingReader. pumpToImpl awaits a read at line3566 and a sink write at line3573. Its shown source cancel call is inside KJ_CATCH at line3597; no separate mid-drop cleanup defer or pumpSettled handling appears in this function.

DrainingReader destruction invokes releaseReader with no JS lock. In that branch the controller clears reader-lock references and retains the locked state; it does not invoke the underlying source cancel algorithm. This is a static local path fact, not an observation of which branch the owned HTTP run executed.

WorkerEntrypoint separately schedules incoming request signal abort as a waitUntil task and drains the request. enable_request_signal creates the controller; request_signal_passthrough determines whether it is ignored by subrequests. Thus signal abort and JS source cancel have distinct wiring.

Official ReadableStream.cancel describes explicit consumer cancellation and the source cancel callback. Incoming request signal docs describe client-cancellation notification/cleanup. The latter does not independently guarantee a particular HTTP/RST path invokes an async source cancel callback within our test deadline.

The pinned existing C++ pending-write regression test gates on its own TestSink write promise and asserts event order: a write is reached, its promise is dropped, then the sink is destroyed. It has no JS source cancel assertion. Its synthetic pending promise establishes a C++ branch condition that an OS send queue alone cannot establish.

inferences.label: candidate only
inferences.text: The observed signal-only/no-source-cancel result is compatible with pump teardown releasing its reader without entering KJ_CATCH. It is not a proof that the current owned run took that path.

inferences.label: unconfirmed
inferences.text: The pending-read-only hypothesis remains unconfirmed. A real kernel send backlog invalidates treating the run as no-pressure, but does not prove the coroutine was suspended in sink->write, which promise was dropped, whether catch was entered, or whether queued cancellation lost its context.

inferences.label: not a gate workaround
inferences.text: Application cleanup explicitly initiated by request.signal may satisfy a separately specified resource cleanup contract. It cannot be relabeled a natural source cancel or set the original cancel KV to observed, and cannot turn the frozen strict test green.

nextMinimumOptions.boundary: Separate owned Linux C++ diagnostic fixture pinned to commit8ea63498; stock/frozen Node and HTTP baseline remains untouched and failing.
nextMinimumOptions.minimalTest: Start from the existing TestSink fixture. Keep the JS source readable. Use an explicit C++ gate to hold the next read in one arm and the sink write promise in another, then drop the actual owning pump promise after the corresponding gate is observed. Record ordered read-entry/read-settle, write-entry/write-settle, KJ_CATCH entry, pump-frame destructor, reader release, sink destructor, real source cancel and request-drain completion. Compare error-returning sink and normal completion separately to detect double or missing cleanup.
nextMinimumOptions.measurement: The pending arm must be established by the actual controlled C++ promise, not bytes enqueued or kernel queue size. Bounded waits, original raw event order and real child/process cleanup must close; timeout/unknown stays failure. No source cancel can be manufactured by a signal hook.
